questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars on the right move first.
Let other traffic pass before you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic pass before you go.
questions.explanation: This sign means you must yield. Slow down and let other vehicles and pedestrians cross in front of you. Stop if needed before you proceed.

questions.question: When you make an emergency roadside stop, you must use your parking brake.
questions.explanation: You should always use your parking brake during an emergency roadside stop. Also turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down when the road is wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: This yellow sign with black markings warns you that the road is slippery when wet. Reduce your speed.

questions.question: A railroad crossing sign should be treated like a yield sign.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing sign, you must yield to any trains or railroad equipment. Treat it like a yield sign.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane is ending. You will need to merge into another lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow sign with black markings warns that a divided highway is starting. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: What color are temporary signs in construction zones?
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones are orange with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle in front moves to the right for you.
When the yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
When the yellow line on the opposite side is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass if it is safe. A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, what should you do?

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop well behind the gates. Wait for the tracks to clear. Then proceed when the gates lift.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates. Wait for the tracks to clear. Then proceed when the gates lift.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when warned by signs, lights, or flaggers. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: You are in an intersection turning left when the light turns red. What should you do?

options.text: Wait in the intersection until the light turns green.
Check for oncoming traffic, then complete your turn.
Make sure it is clear, then back up out of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic, then complete your turn.
questions.explanation: If you entered the intersection while the light was green, you may finish turning left even after the light turns red. Yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign marks the start of a no passing zone.

questions.question: In cities, drivers leaving an alley, building, private road, or driveway do not need to stop completely if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Drivers leaving an alley, building, private road, or driveway must come to a complete stop and yield to other drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
Brake hard and steer to the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly and take your foot off the accelerator. Let the vehicle slow down. Apply the brakes gently when safe. Do not move to the shoulder until the car has slowed considerably.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield to drivers who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to drivers who arrived before you. Wait your turn to enter the intersection.

questions.question: Which statement about drinking and driving is true?

options.text: If you can walk straight after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal blood alcohol limit, your driving is not impaired.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. You need good judgment to drive safely. Even below the legal limit, any amount of alcohol can reduce your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and hazardous material trucks.
Watch for trains coming from both directions.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with caution. Look for trains from both directions. Watch for vehicles like school buses and hazardous material trucks that must stop at all railroad crossings.

questions.question: A school bus ahead has flashing lights and an extended signal arm. What should you do?

options.text: Drive 15 mph if no children are present.
Drive at normal speed, but watch for children.

questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing lights and an extended signal arm, you must come to a complete stop. Stay stopped until the arm is pulled back and the bus moves. This applies whether you are traveling in the same direction or from the opposite direction.

questions.question: Is it safe to stop on railroad tracks for a short time while moving with other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Never stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Only cross railroad tracks if your entire vehicle will fit on the other side.

questions.question: Can only vehicles with disability plates or placards park in reserved disability spaces?
questions.explanation: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities spaces may only be used by vehicles with disability license plates, Disabled Veteran license plates, or disabled parking placards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The right lane ends soon. Merge left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends soon. Merge left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the number of lanes is reducing ahead and traffic must merge left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: When you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs warn you of workers, slow-moving equipment, and closed lanes ahead. Reduce your speed and be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go the opposite direction where this sign is posted.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle or property, leave a note with your name, phone number, and address securely attached to the vehicle or property you hit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a left turn. It is unsafe and illegal to turn left where this sign is posted.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull to the right edge of the road and stop. Position yourself parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, move toward the nearest road edge.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and collision severity relate to a vehicle's speed?
questions.explanation: Higher speeds cause more serious collisions. As speed increases, stopping distance increases and collision impact increases, raising the risk of serious injury or death. Increase your following distance as your speed increases.
